# User guide: Settings reference

## In plain words

The plugin keeps its settings on one page: **AI CLI Agents**, under Unraid's **Settings** menu. The page has six tabs: **Configuration**, **Agent Store**, **Storage**, **Config Hub**, **Agent Relay** and **Debug Console**. This page lists every control on those tabs, in the order the page shows them, with the label the page shows. A few switches live in the terminal drawer instead: voice, the microphone and the pin. They are at the end of this page.

On the Configuration tab, the help for each setting is behind an **(i)** button next to its label. Tap or click the button, or press Enter, to read what the setting does. Move the mouse over it to see the help for a moment. Press Escape or tap outside to close it.

Each card on the Configuration tab has a header with the same parts. Select the title or the arrow to close the card or open it again. The line in the header shows the main facts of the card, for example **Dark · 14 px**, so a closed card still tells you something. The **(i)** button in the header explains the whole card. The three-dot button opens a small menu with **Move up**, **Move down**, **Move to top**, **Collapse all**, **Expand all** and **Reset layout**. The same **Reset layout** button is at the top of the tab.

To move a card, open its three-dot menu and select **Move up**, **Move down** or **Move to top**. An item is grey when the card cannot move that way, for example **Move up** on the first card. With the keyboard, put the focus on the three-dot button and press Alt and the up or down arrow key. A screen reader says, for example, "Card Storage moved up. Position 2 of 9." On a computer with a mouse you can also press the three-dot button, hold it and drag the card to a new place. Move the pointer more than a few pixels to start the drag. A short click still opens the menu. The other cards stay still until you let go. Press Escape to cancel the drag. On a phone or tablet there is no drag: use the menu. Your browser remembers the order. **Reset layout** puts the cards back in their first order. Your browser remembers which cards are closed. Nothing about this goes to the server. A card whose status is **Off** starts closed the first time. A card that shows a warning, for example a storage move that needs attention, opens by itself.

Most controls save at once, with no Save button. The note **Changes save as you make them.** at the top of the Configuration tab says so. After a save, a short **Saved** mark appears next to the control for two seconds, and the status line of the card follows the new value. A screen reader says "Saved". A dialog appears only when a change is refused, or when a change needs your confirm first, because it moves data or closes workspaces. Each table says what happens at once when a control changes. The last column says whether an agent may change the setting through the Plugin management tools. An agent can only do that when you turn on **Let agents manage the plugin** on the Configuration tab.

## How to read the tables

| Column | Meaning |
| :-- | :-- |
| Setting | The label on the page, in bold where it is a label. |
| What it does | The effect of the setting, in plain words. |
| Default | The value a fresh install uses. |
| Allowed values | The choices, or the range the page accepts. |
| When to change it | The case where a different value helps. |
| At once | What happens the moment you change the control. |
| Agent | Yes when an agent may change this setting with the Plugin management tools (the setting **Let agents manage the plugin**). No when only a person may. |

Three outcomes appear often in the "At once" column:

- **Saves, nothing else.** The page shows a short "Saved" message. Nothing restarts and the page does not reload.
- **Page reloads.** The page reloads itself after the save.
- **Confirm dialog.** A dialog explains what will happen. If you press **Cancel**, press Escape or click outside the dialog, the setting returns to its old value. Nothing moves.

On a phone, the tables on this page scroll sideways. The controls on the page are large enough to touch.

## Configuration tab

The Configuration tab shows eleven cards: **General**, **Storage**, **Terminal**, **Automatic continue**, **Relay notices**, **Agent voice**, **Dictation**, **Notebook**, **Script runs**, **Sub-agent workspaces** and **SSH keys**. On a wide screen the page spreads the cards over several columns. On a phone it shows one column. Most cards have two parts. The main settings are always in view. The seldom-used settings are in the **Advanced** part, a section that you open when you need it. In this guide, each setting is under its card, and the rows of the **Advanced** part come after the heading **Advanced**.

### General card

Choose where the plugin shows and which user your agents run as, so it fits your server.

The status line shows whether the tab is shown, the Terminal user and the Starting folder, for example **Tab shown: Yes · user root · /mnt/user**.

| Setting | What it does | Default | Allowed values | When to change it | At once | Agent |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| **Show the AI CLI Agents tab** | Shows or hides the tab in Unraid's top menu. The plugin keeps running when the tab is hidden. | Yes | Yes, No | Choose No when you want the terminal tab out of the menu and you reach the plugin from Settings only. | Saves. The menu changes when Unraid next loads a page. | No |
| **Terminal user** | The Unraid user account that agents run as. Each user has its own home, files and settings. Changing it reloads the page. The two buttons next to it add a user (opens the Unraid page for that) and refresh the page. | root | Any Unraid user in the list | Change it when you want agents to run as a normal user and not as root. | Saves. **The page reloads**, because the workspaces and arguments belong to the user's home. | No |
| **Starting folder** | The folder a new terminal or file browser opens in. The folder button next to it lets you browse. | /mnt/user | A folder path | Change it to the share where your projects live. | Saves. | No |
| **Largest upload** | The largest file you can drop or paste into a workspace, in megabytes. The page shows the hint "MB · 0 = no limit". | 512 MB | A whole number of megabytes. 0 means no limit | Raise it for large files. Lower it to protect the RAM disk. | Saves. | Yes |

#### Advanced

The **Advanced** part of the card is closed at first. Select **Advanced** to open it. Its **(i)** button says what is inside. It holds the log detail, the version checks, the switch that lets agents manage the plugin, your name in the records and the name of this browser.

| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| **Log detail** | How much the plugin writes to its log on the Debug Console. "Errors only" is the quietest. "Debug" helps when you report a problem and writes the most. | Normal | Errors only; Warnings; Normal; Debug | Choose Debug while you look for a fault. Go back to Normal afterwards, because Debug writes much more. | Saves. New log lines follow the level. | No |
| **Check for new agent versions** | How often the plugin looks online for new versions of the installed agents. "Never" turns the check off. "Check for updates" on the Agent Store still works. | Daily at 6am | Every 6 hours; Daily at 6am; Weekly (Monday 6am); Never | Choose Never on a server with no internet. Check by hand with **Check for Updates** on the Agent Store tab. | Saves. The plugin changes its schedule job at once. | No |
| **Keep version check results for** | How long the plugin keeps old results of the version check. Older results are removed. | 3 months | 1 month; 3 months; 6 months; 12 months | Choose a longer time when you want more past versions in the version lists. | Saves. | No |
| **Let agents manage the plugin** | Gives agents tools to read the plugin's state and make routine changes. Reads change nothing. Changes appear in the Activity tray. Refused calls appear together in one short-lived row. Delete, upgrade, back up, restore and merge only propose, and wait for your approval in the Manager. See [Plugin management tools for agents](agent-tools.md). | Off (default) | On; Off (default) | Turn it on when you want an agent to help you manage the plugin. | Saves. The plugin adds or removes the tools for the agents at once. | **Your name in the records** | The name that follows your Unraid login in the Activity tray, the event list and the log. For example, "root (John)". The login always shows, so this name only adds to it. | Empty | Text, up to 40 characters | Set it when more than one person uses the same Unraid login, so the records say who acted. | Saves. New records use it at once. Old records keep their text. | No. Only a person can change it. |
| **Device name (this browser)** | Names this browser in the Activity tray, so you can see which device did what. The name stays in this browser. For example: phone or laptop. | Empty | Text, up to 40 characters | Set it when you use the plugin from several devices and want the activity record to say which one acted. | Saves in this browser only. ### Storage card

Keep your agents' settings, logins and history safe, and keep the boot disk free.

The status line shows the kind of storage of the homes and of the agents, for example **Homes: Plain folders · Agents: Compressed layers**.

| Setting | What it does | Default | Allowed values | When to change it | At once | Agent |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| **Home storage** | Chooses how the plugin stores every home. Compressed layers save space on a small boot disk and protect a USB stick from wear. Plain folders need no saves or tidy-ups. The drop-down shows what is true on disk: **Plain folders**, **Compressed layers**, or **Mixed: 1 plain, 2 compressed**. Choosing another value does not start anything: the drop-down turns orange and the button **Apply: convert …** appears under it. Pressing **Apply** converts the data, and you are asked first. If every home already uses one form but the setting names the other, the button reads **Apply: make new homes plain folders too** (or **compressed layers**) and only saves the setting. New homes use this setting. | Compressed layers | Compressed layers; Plain folders | Choose Plain folders only when you need ordinary folders on a drive that is not USB flash. Layers reduce wear on flash. When the drop-down shows Mixed, choose a mode and press **Apply** to convert the other homes. | Before it closes sessions, the confirmation checks space for the new storage and the copies needed to restore the old storage. It converts only the homes that are not on the new choice. It compares that total with current free space and keeps at least 2 GB or 10% of each destination disk free. When it refuses, it gives the required and available space and saves the message in the status. After it starts, an inline status names the kind and shows the target and progress. The **Storage** tab also shows progress and disables conflicting actions. You can change pages while it runs; manual and automatic workspace starts wait until it ends. The migration waits for any agent installation already running. New installs, upgrades, restores from a kept agent backup and removals are refused until it ends. Automatic saves, merges and queued storage jobs also wait until conversion ends. | No |
| **Agent storage** | Chooses how the plugin stores every agent. Compressed layers save space on a small boot disk and protect a USB stick from wear. Plain folders need no saves or tidy-ups. The drop-down shows what is true on disk, in the same words as **Home storage**. A change waits for the button **Apply**, in the same way. Pressing **Apply** converts the data, and you are asked first. New agent installs and updates use this setting. | Compressed layers on a USB boot stick; Plain folders on an internal boot disk | Compressed layers; Plain folders | Choose Compressed layers when the boot disk is small. Compressed layers use less space. Choose Plain folders when the boot disk has room and you want simple folders. A USB boot stick should keep layers. | The same checks and the same status as **Home storage**, for the agents only. The agents that are not on the new choice convert; the others stay. | No |
| **Where homes are stored** | The disk or pool that holds the homes of every user. **Change…** moves them. You are asked first, and the move runs in the background. | /boot/config/plugins/unraid-aicliagents/persistence (the flash drive) | A folder the picker lists as available, or a custom path | Move it to a cache pool for speed and space. See [Home and agent storage](storage.md). | **Change…** opens a picker. **Move storage here** starts the storage move. A confirm dialog "Migrate Storage?" follows. A queued or running storage conversion (**Home storage** or **Agent storage**) blocks the move. Old or replaced home data appears under **Left over** on **Boot disk space** after the move. See "Warning dialogs" below. | No |
| **Where agents are stored** | The disk or pool that holds the installed agents. **Change…** moves them. You are asked first. | /boot/config/plugins/unraid-aicliagents/persistence (the flash drive) | A folder the picker lists as available, or a custom path | Move it to a cache pool or an Unassigned Device when the flash drive is small. | The same as **Where homes are stored**. | No |
| **Keep the previous agent version** | After an upgrade, the plugin keeps the last version so you can go back. Turn this off to keep only the version in use and free space on the boot disk. | Yes | Yes; No | Choose No when the boot disk is nearly full and you do not need to roll back. | None. The plugin removes the previous version at its next clean-up. A version that a workspace uses always stays. | No |

#### Advanced

The **Advanced** part of the card is closed at first. Select **Advanced** to open it. Its **(i)** button says what is inside. It holds the save schedule, the merge limit, the work folder, the caches, the temporary files and the path that a workspace runs on.

| Setting | What it does | Default | Allowed values | When to change it | At once | Agent |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| **Save unsaved home changes every** (with the **Save now** button) | The page hides this row when every home is a plain folder, because a plain folder has nothing to save. A home in compressed layers collects changes in memory. This is how often the plugin saves them to disk. **Save now** saves the home of the Terminal user at once. This is not a backup: the backup is on the Storage tab, on the home card. | Every 2 hours | Every 15 minutes; Every 30 minutes; Every hour; Every 2 hours; Every 4 hours; Every 8 hours; Every 12 hours; Once a day | Choose a shorter interval when you use the RAM writable layer and want less to lose on a crash. Choose a longer one to reduce writes to USB flash. | Saves. The **Save now** button shows a confirm dialog first ("Persist Home Changes?"). | No |
| **Where unsaved changes are kept** | Changes to a home wait in memory or on disk until the next save. Memory is fast and causes no disk wear, but a crash loses the unsaved changes. Disk keeps them through a crash or a power cut. A change waits for the button **Apply: move the writable layer to RAM** (or **to disk**). Pressing **Apply** closes open workspaces, saves the changes, and reopens the home. You are asked first. | Memory (zram): fast, no disk wear, lost on a crash until saved | Memory (zram): fast, no disk wear, lost on a crash until saved; Disk: survives a crash or power cut, uses space on the persistence drive | Choose Disk when you cannot afford to lose work on a crash or a power cut and the persistence drive has room. | Confirm dialog "Move the writable layer to RAM?" or "Move the writable layer to disk?". See "Warning dialogs" below. | No |
| **Merge layers after** | Each save of a home adds one layer. Many layers make the first open slower. When a home reaches this number, the plugin merges them into one layer. Default 30. Merging starts at 28, or sooner when the disk is nearly full. Agents always use one layer. | 30 layers | A whole number from 4 to 40 | Raise it for fewer merges. Lower it for a faster first load of a home. | Saves. | No |
| **Work folder for storage jobs** | A storage job (a merge, a conversion, a move) needs a place for temporary copies when the boot disk is full. A merge uses it for database copies, and a conversion to plain folders uses it for the copy of the home and the old layers. Leave this empty and the plugin picks a folder on a pool. It never uses memory or the boot disk. | Empty: the plugin chooses a folder (Docker appdata, then VM domains, then a protected pool) | Empty, or a full folder path that is not on the boot disk, in RAM or in `/tmp` | Set it when you want these copies on one disk of your choice. | Saves. A value that points to the boot disk, RAM or `/tmp` is not saved. | No |
| **Caches of plain-folder homes** | Tools such as npm and pip keep downloaded files in caches. A cache is only a copy. A tool downloads it again when it is gone. | Memory | **Memory** or **A folder on a pool** | Keep Memory unless your caches are large and you have a fast pool. | Saves. A running home keeps its caches until it starts again. | No |

### Terminal card

Make the terminal easy to read, and keep typing fast when the server is busy.

The status line shows the colour scheme and the text size, for example **Dark · 14 px**. The card has no **Advanced** part.

| Setting | What it does | Default | Allowed values | When to change it | At once | Agent |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| **Colour scheme** | The colours of the terminal windows. Dark is the default. | Dark | Dark; Light; Solarized | Change it to match your Unraid theme or your eyes. | Saves. A terminal window that is open keeps its colours until the page reloads. | Yes |
| **Text size** | The size of the text in the terminal windows, in pixels. 12 to 16 is usual. | 14 | A whole number from 8 to 32 | Raise it for a large screen or a phone. Lower it to see more text. | Saves. A terminal window that is open keeps its size until the page reloads. | Yes |
| **Keep typing fast when the server is busy** | Gives the Unraid web page and the terminals a higher priority than the plugin's own background work. Typing in a terminal then stays quick while the server is busy. Docker containers, virtual machines and the array are not changed, and the agents keep the normal priority. Off puts everything back. | Off (default) | On; Off (default) | Choose On when typing in a terminal lags while Plex, a virtual machine or a backup runs. | Saves and applies at once, without a restart. Off puts every changed program back at once. Unraid can restart its web server and start its programs again at the normal priority. The plugin raises them again within five minutes. | No |

### Automatic continue card

Let an agent carry on by itself after a restart or a temporary error, so you do not have to type "continue".

The status line shows the two switches, for example **After a restart: On · After a model error: Verified agents**.

| Setting | What it does | Default | Allowed values | When to change it | At once | Agent |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| **Continue after a restart** | When the plugin restarts a workspace (after a server restart, an agent upgrade or a reload), the agent is told to continue its work. A plain page reload does not do this. On by default. | On (default) | On (default); Off | Choose Off when you want to read the screen first and start each agent yourself. | Saves. | Yes |
| **Continue after a model error** | When the AI service answers with a temporary error (for example "overloaded") and the agent stops, the plugin types "Continue" for you. "Verified agents" are the agents the plugin has tested. | Verified agents (default) | Verified agents (default); All agents; Off | Choose All agents when you use an agent that is not on the verified list. The verified agents are OpenCode, Kilo Code, Claude Code, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI and Qwen Code. Choose Off to stop the automatic Continue. | Saves. To stop one planned Continue, cancel the clock tag on the workspace. | Yes |
| **Wait before each continue, and how many** | The minutes to wait before the first, second and third continue for the same error, for example 1,5,15, and how many continues the plugin types for one error. After the last one, the Activity tray says the workspace needs you. The page shows the hint "minutes · times". | 1,5,15 minutes; at most 3 times | Wait: one to three whole minutes from 1 to 120, separated by commas. Times: a whole number from 0 to 10 | Use longer waits when the provider is slow to recover. Use 0 times to turn the repeat off for every error. | Saves. | Yes |

#### Advanced

The **Advanced** part of the card is closed at first. Select **Advanced** to open it. Its **(i)** button says what is inside. It holds your own patterns, the built-in patterns and the Terminal input safety rules.

##### Your patterns and the built-in patterns

The card holds the screen messages that mean "the agent stopped on a temporary error and may continue" (a temporary model error, or a usage quota with a retry time). Add your own when an agent stops on a message the plugin does not know. Each change saves at once. The card has no setting that an agent changes directly. An agent may propose one pattern with a tool, and the pattern then shows in your list as "added by an agent".

| Control | What it does | Default | Allowed values | At once |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| **Your patterns** list, with a switch, **Edit**, **Report** and **Delete** on each row | Turns a pattern on or off, edits it, prepares a report for the plugin authors, or deletes it. | Empty | Not applicable | The switch saves at once. **Delete** asks you to confirm in the row. **Report** opens a prefilled report page that you review and send yourself. A saved pattern that the plugin now refuses stays in the list with the switch off and the note "Not in use" with the reason. Edit or delete it. |
| **Add pattern** | Opens a dialog with the fields below. | Not applicable | Not applicable | Opens the dialog. |
| **Name** | Names the pattern. | Empty | Text, up to 60 characters | Part of the dialog. |
| **Agent** | Chooses which agent the pattern is for. | All agents | All agents, or one installed agent | Part of the dialog. |
| **Kind** | Chooses what the pattern means. | Transient error | Transient error; Usage quota with retry time; Busy marker; Chrome (status line) | Part of the dialog. A Transient error expression must start with ^. A Usage quota expression needs a capture group that holds the retry time. A Busy marker shows that the agent still works. A Chrome line is a status or footer line that is not new output. |
| **Regular expression** | The text pattern. | Empty | A PCRE expression, written as /body/flags or only the body (saved as /body/iu) | Part of the dialog. |
| **Sample (the screen lines this is for)** | The exact screen lines the pattern is for. The expression must match the sample before you can save. Secrets in the sample are masked. | Empty | Text | Part of the dialog. |
| **Test against a workspace screen** (with **Workspace**) | Reads the screen of a running workspace and shows which lines match. | Not applicable | A running workspace | Shows the result in the dialog. Nothing is typed. |
| **Save**, **Report this pattern**, **Close** | Saves the pattern, prepares a report, or closes the dialog. | Not applicable | Not applicable | **Save** saves the pattern at once. |
| **Built-in patterns (read-only)** | Lists the patterns that ship with the plugin, by agent and kind. | The built-in list | Not applicable | You cannot change it. |

##### Terminal input safety rules

This is a section inside the **Advanced** part of the Automatic continue card. Before the plugin types into an agent, it reads the bottom of the screen. A block rule stops the typing when the screen shows a question, a menu or a pager. An idle rule says what the empty prompt of an agent looks like. Rules are regular expressions (text patterns), written as /body/flags. A rule that does not compile is ignored and the built-in rule stays.

| Control | What it does | Default | When to use it | At once |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| **Block rules (all agents)** list, **Add block rule** | Adds a rule that holds input for every agent. | The built-in rules | Add one when the plugin types into a screen where it should wait. | The rule joins the list. It is not saved until you press **Save rules**. |
| **Idle rules for** (choose an agent), **Add idle rule** | Adds a rule that matches the empty prompt of the chosen agent. | None, unless the agent has built-in idle rules | Add one when the plugin never types into an agent that is waiting at its prompt. | The same as the block rules. |
| **Save rules** | Saves the lists. | Not applicable | After you add or remove a rule. | Saves the rules. |
| **Discard changes** | Puts the lists back to the saved state. | Not applicable | When you change your mind. | The lists reload. |
| **Workspace to test**, **Check screen now** | Reads the screen of one running workspace and shows whether the rules hold or allow input. | Not applicable | After you change a rule. | Shows the result next to the button. Nothing is typed. |

The status line shows the wording of the notice and the resend time, for example **Short · resend after 10 min**.

The link **Show example** under the list shows the line for an actor and for a direct message. | Short (default): about 20 words | Short (default): about 20 words; Minimal: about 10 words; Full: the long original text; Custom: my own words | Choose Minimal to save the most tokens. Choose Custom to use your own wording. | Saves after the page checks the text. The example opens at once when a custom text is refused, with the reason. A custom text that does not pass the check is not saved. | No |
| **Custom Relay notice text** (shown when the wording is Custom) | Holds your own notice text. It is one line of up to 300 characters. It must contain the two markers {what} and {command}, and it must end with at least 8 plain characters after the last marker. The plugin adds [Relay] in front. Text from a sender is never inserted. | Empty | See "What it does" | Use it when the built-in wordings do not fit your agents. | Saves after the check, as above. | No |
| **Resend a notice after** | After one notice, the plugin waits for the agent to read its inbox. If it has not read it after this time, the plugin types the notice again. The page shows the hint "minutes · 1 to 240". | 10 minutes | A whole number from 1 to 240 | Raise it for agents that work for long periods without reading. | Saves. | No |

#### Advanced

### Agent voice card

Hear your agent when it needs you, so you can look away from the screen. An agent can speak to get your attention. By default it uses your browser's voice. Set up a voice server for a natural voice.

The status line shows whether voice is on and the voice server, for example **On · voice server voice.example**. The main settings are a **Natural voice** row, the **Voice** switch and the text-to-speech engine fields. The **Advanced** part holds the **Voice mail** limits. The guide [Voice](voice.md) explains the whole feature. Voice fields save one at a time, when you leave the field. A short "Saved." message shows next to the field.

The page waits until the engine answers, then saves the engine address and plays a test sentence. **Cancel** stops the wait. | No |
| **Voice** | Turns speech on or off for every open tab on every device. To mute one workspace, use its "…" menu in the terminal drawer. The same switch is the speaker icon in the terminal drawer. | Off | On; Off | Turn it on to let agents speak to you. | Saves. Every open tab updates. When you turn it on, this tab plays a confirmation. | Yes |

The voice list reloads from the engine. | No. An agent cannot change the address. |

### Script runs card

Let your own scripts on this server start an agent for you, while you stay in control of what each script may do. The card **Script runs** lets a script on the server start an agent with the command `aicli-run`. See [Run an agent from a script](script-runs.md). No agent can change any of these settings. The status line shows the switch and the number of authorised scripts. It also shows the number that need attention, for example **On · 2 scripts · 1 needs attention**.

| Setting | What it does | Default | Allowed values | When to change it | At once | Agent |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| **Let scripts start agent runs** | With On, a script on the list can start an agent. With Off, the command refuses every call and creates nothing. | Off (default) | On; Off (default) | Turn it on when you add your first script. | Saves, nothing else. | No |
| **Authorised scripts** | Each entry shows its name and description. Select an entry to see its file, fingerprint, agents, folders, mode and runs each day, and to edit or remove it. A changed file is refused until you trust it again. A script path under `/tmp` is refused because it is temporary. A script can also ask for its own entry with `aicli-run --request-access`; the request waits in the Activity tray until you approve it. A read-only run starts at once. A run that may change files waits for your approval in the Activity tray. The agent runs as root. | Empty | **Add a script**; in the dialog: **Edit**, **Save**, **Cancel**, **Remove**, **Trust the file as it is now**, **Switch to the original and trust it as it is now** | Add a script for each job. | Saves when you press **Save**. | No |

| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |

| **Runs each day** | The most runs that start in 24 hours, for all scripts. | 6 | 1 to 500 | Raise it for a busy server. | Saves, nothing else. | No |
| **Wait before the same problem runs again** | A script can name a problem with a key. The same key starts no new run for this many hours. | 24 hours | 0 to 720 | Lower it when a problem needs a quick second look. | Saves, nothing else. | No |
| **Time to approve a run** | A run that may change files waits for your approval. With no answer in this time, it ends and starts nothing. | 24 hours | 1 to 168 | Raise it when you look at the Activity tray rarely. | Saves, nothing else. | No |
| **Time limit for a run** | The plugin closes a run that has not reported when this time passes. It keeps the result and the Notebook card. | 60 minutes | 1 to 1440 | Raise it for a long check. | Saves, nothing else. | No |
| **Notify me when a run starts and ends** | Raises an Unraid notice when a run starts or reports done. Warnings, for example a refused script, always show. | Yes (default) | Yes (default); No | Turn it off for a script that runs often. | Saves, nothing else. | No |
| **Folder for temporary run folders** | The folder that holds the temporary folders of runs that a script starts with `--temp`. Empty means the appdata folder of Unraid on its pool, plus `_tmp/aicliagents-runs`. | Empty (default) | A full path inside a share of a pool. A path under `/mnt/user`, or a new top-level folder on a pool, is not stored | Change it only when you want these folders on another pool. | Saves. The next run that asks for a temporary folder uses it. | No |

Each start shows in the Activity tray and names the agent that asked. See [Plugin management tools for agents](agent-tools.md). The switches are off by default. No agent can change these settings. The card has no **Advanced** part. The status line shows, for example, **Off · up to 6 in total**, and a card that is **Off** starts closed.

Each start shows in the Activity tray and names the agent that asked. See [Plugin management tools for agents](agent-tools.md). | Off (default) | On; Off (default) | Turn it on when you want an agent to hand a task to a second agent. It also needs **Let agents manage the plugin**, in **General**, part **Advanced**. An agent can start a workspace that already exists when this switch is **Off (default)**. | Saves. The tools answer at once. | No. An agent cannot turn the switch on or raise a limit. |

A number outside the range becomes the default. | No |

Open an agent's terminal straight from your own computer with ssh, with no browser. Add your public key, then run `ssh <user> aicli-agent-<name>`. The key can run only that command.

| Public key box and **Label** field | Hold the key you paste (one line that starts with ssh-ed25519 or ssh-rsa) and a name for it. | Empty. The label becomes "Unnamed key" when you leave it empty | Nothing, until you press **Add Key**. |

The card has no **Advanced** part.

## Warning dialogs

Three Configuration settings move stored data. Each one shows a dialog before anything moves. In each dialog, **Cancel**, the Escape key and a click outside the dialog all put the setting back. A click outside the dialog does not close it by accident. Nothing moves until you press the confirm button.

| Dialog | Opens from | What it warns about | Confirm button |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| Change home storage? / Change agent storage? | **Home storage** or **Agent storage** | The homes (or the agents) that are not on the new choice will change. Items of the other kind do not change. Before it closes sessions, the dialog uses a complete **Boot disk space** report from the last 10 minutes and checks current free space for both new storage and rollback copies. It keeps at least 2 GB or 10% of each destination disk free. It refuses when the report is missing, old or incomplete, or when any disk would use its reserve. The refusal shows the required and available space and stays in the status. Existing sessions close safely after the check passes. Moving to plain folders keeps the old SquashFS data in a migration archive. Moving to compressed layers archives the plain folders only after the new layer and its manifest check out. The migration waits for an agent installation already in progress. New installs, upgrades, restores from a kept agent backup and removals are refused until it ends. When the storage is removable or USB, the dialog adds that compressed layers are recommended to reduce wear, and plain folders on USB need your acknowledgement. | **Convert homes** or **Convert agents** |
| Move the writable layer to RAM? / Move the writable layer to disk? | **Where unsaved changes are kept** | RAM is fast and wears no disk, but changes made since the last save are lost if the server crashes or loses power. Disk survives a crash or a power cut and uses space on the persistence drive. The dialog lists each home, how many megabytes move, and warns that your open workspaces are closed while the data moves. This can take several minutes. Do not reload the page or restart the server meanwhile. The plugin refuses the move when the drive has too little room, when the RAM layer device is too small, or when the home storage is on USB flash (disk is not offered there). The plugin refuses the setting for the Plain directories engine, which has no writable layer. | **Close workspaces and move** (or **Save setting** when no home needs to move). The dialog opens when you press **Apply**. **Cancel** keeps your choice in the drop-down. |
| Migrate Storage? | **Where homes are stored** or **Where agents are stored**, after **Move storage here** | Files are saved and merged before they move. For homes, the move also carries plain home data and unsaved changes. It checks the copy before it changes the path. When old home data exists to copy, different data already at the target stays in a dated archive. The dialog lists the old and the new path, the number of items and the total size. When the new path stays on /mnt/user, the dialog also warns that heavy save or merge work through the Unraid share layer can slow or freeze the whole server, and it suggests a pool path (/mnt/cache/…), an Unassigned Device path (/mnt/disks/…) or a single-disk path (/mnt/diskN/…). /mnt/user is acceptable when nothing else is available. | **Yes, Migrate** |

After a successful move the page reloads. A busy result leaves the old path active. The Activity tray says either "The old home mount is still busy" or "Home storage is busy. Try again in a moment." Close any remaining workspaces, or wait for the home mount to finish, then select **Move storage here** again. For any other failed move, the setting returns to its old value and the dialog says why.

## Agent Store tab

The tab shows one card per agent under the heading **AI Agent Marketplace**. Each card has a header row with the icon, the name, one line of status, the version you run and, when the channel offers another one, the new version as a button that opens the dialog **Update <agent>**, an (i) button (description, release notes, install method, package name), the button **Install** (or **Upgrade**, which shows when you point at the card), and a **...** menu to update, open the release notes, and move or close the card. The foot of an installed card has the links **Remove old versions (frees N)** and **Uninstall (frees N)**. See [Agent Store](agent-store.md).

| Control | What it does | Default | Allowed values | At once |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| **Check for updates** (with a status line such as "Checked 7 min ago") | Asks online for the newest version of every agent. The status line shows when the plugin last checked. | Not applicable | Not applicable | Starts a check. |
| **Search agents…** | Filters the cards by name. | Empty | Text | Filters as you type. |
| **All**, **Installed**, **Updates** | Shows all agents, only installed agents, or only agents with an update. | All | All; Installed; Updates | Filters the cards. |
| **A–Z** / **Z–A** button | Reverses the order of the cards. | A–Z | A–Z; Z–A | Reorders the cards. |

Every installed agent card has five panels, opened with the chips **Version**, **Variables**, **Storage**, **Terminal** and **Start options**. The (i) at the end of the row explains them. A card for an agent that is not installed has only the **Version** chip active. The other four become available after you install the agent. A coloured dot on a chip shows that it holds settings: amber means a field the agent needs is empty, green means all are set, and a custom colour means you changed the defaults.

### Version panel

| Setting | What it does | Default | Allowed values | When to change it | At once | Agent |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| **Release channel** | Chooses which releases the agent follows. Stable gets tested releases. Beta gets newer releases that may be less tested. Pinned locks the agent to one version until you pick another. | Stable | Stable; Beta; Pinned. Beta shows only for agents installed from npm or from GitHub releases | Choose Beta to try new features early. Choose Pinned when a version works for you and you want no change. | Saves. The version list reloads for the channel. Nothing installs. | Yes |
| **Version** | Lists the versions of the channel and the kept backups of past versions. Picking a version installs it. Picking a kept backup restores it. | The installed version | A version in the list | Pick an older version to roll back. | Picking a version starts the install or the restore. A restore shows a confirm dialog. The restore takes a snapshot of the current version first, so you can undo it. | No |
| **Install** / **Upgrade** / **Uninstall** buttons (card header) | Install the latest version of the channel, upgrade to it, or remove the agent. | Not applicable | Not applicable | Use them to manage the agent. | Install and Upgrade show progress on the card. **Uninstall** removes the agent. | Upgrade: proposal only |

### Variables panel

| Setting | What it does | Default | When to change it | At once |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| Agent fields (for example an API key) | The agent's own settings, set as environment variables each time the agent starts. Password fields show •••••••• when a value exists. Leave •••••••• untouched to keep the value. Empty a field to delete it. | Empty | Enter the key or choice the agent needs. | **Save** writes the values. A running agent reads them at its next start. |
| **Variables** (with **Add variable**) | General environment variables for the agent, as name and value pairs. A workspace's own **ENV** tab wins over these for the same name. | None | Add a variable that every workspace of this agent needs. | **Save** writes them. |

| **Max RAM (MB)** (Node-based agents only) | Caps the memory of the Node process the agent runs in. | 4096 | A whole number from 512 to 65536, in steps of 512 | Raise it if the agent stops with an out-of-memory message. | Saves when you leave the field. The agent uses it at its next start. | Yes |

### Terminal panel

The panel lists tmux settings (tmux is the session manager that keeps a terminal alive on the server). The settings apply every time this agent starts in any workspace. A workspace may override each one from its own drawer. The panel saves by itself half a second after a change and shows "Saved". A dot marks a value that differs from the built-in default. **Reset all to built-in** puts every value back to the built-in default.

| Setting | What it does | Default | Allowed values |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| status | Shows the status bar at the bottom of the terminal. | off | on; off |
| mouse | Turns on mouse support: click to select, drag to resize, scroll for history. | off | on; off |
| history-limit | Sets the lines of scrollback per pane. A higher value uses more memory. | 10000 | A number |
| prefix | Sets the command prefix key. | C-b | A key name |
| base-index | Sets the number of the first window. | 0 | A number |
| bell-action | Chooses which pane raises a bell alert. | any | any; none; current; other |
| default-terminal | Sets the TERM value the programs see. | tmux-256color | Text |
| focus-events | Passes focus gained and lost codes to programs (vim needs this to reload files). | on | on; off |
| allow-passthrough | Lets escape sequences pass through, for inline images and links. | on | on; off |
| escape-time | Sets the wait after the Escape key, in milliseconds. | 0 | A number |
| set-clipboard | Lets programs set the clipboard. | on | Text (tmux accepts on, external and off) |
| extended-keys | Turns on extended key codes. | off | Text (tmux accepts on, off and always) |
| window-size | Decides how the window is sized when several devices are attached. | latest | Text |

The panel also has a section **Keep saved workspaces running**.

| Setting | What it does | Default | When to change it | At once |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| **Restart all saved workspaces** | When on, all saved workspaces of this agent start after a reboot and are recreated if their agent exits. It also relaunches them after a plugin upgrade. | Off | Turn it on for agents that must always run. | Saves ("Saved ✓"). An agent may change it through the tool for auto-launch. |
| **Start fresh if no resume** | When no earlier conversation can resume, discard the saved session state and start a brand-new session. Turning off the first switch also clears this one. | Off | Turn it on when a failed resume should not block a start. | Saves. |

### Start options panel

| Setting | What it does | Default | Allowed values | When to change it | At once |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| **CLI Arguments** (agent-wide default) | Extra flags added to the agent's launch command. A workspace sets its own on top in the drawer. | Empty | Flags as text. The page rejects a semicolon, a pipe, an ampersand, a backtick and a dollar sign | Add a flag that every workspace of the agent needs. | **Save** writes the flags. The agent uses them at its next start. |

## Storage tab

See [Home and agent storage](storage.md) and [Home backup and restore](backup-restore.md). The tab is a list of cards. Every card has the same header as the cards of the Configuration tab: a button that opens and closes the card, a one-line status, an **(i)** with help, and a menu (**Move up**, **Move down**, **Move to top**, **Collapse all**, **Expand all**, **Reset layout**). The order and the open state are saved in this browser only. The cards start in this order: the homes, **Boot disk space**, **RAM disk**.

The card **RAM disk** shows how full the RAM disk of Unraid is (if it fills up, Unraid, the plugin and the running agents can stop working), for example "41 % of 7.8 GB used". It is closed while the use is under 80 %. It has no setting.

**Homes** shows one card for each home, titled **Home:** and the user name. The status line of a home reads, for example, "Plain folders on the boot disk · no saves needed" or "12 layers · 240 MB unsaved". A banner at the top of the tab shows a storage problem or a running merge. While a merge runs, storage actions pause. Workspaces of that home resume by themselves when it ends.

### Boot disk space card: archive and remove

The card **Boot disk space** (see [Home and agent storage](storage.md), "Boot disk space") has four lines that offer **Archive…** and **Remove**. A line shows only while it has something to move. A small **(i)** beside the name of the line gives a short note.

| Control | What it does | At once | Agent |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| **Home** *name*: **quarantine** | Counts the damaged agent databases that the plugin set aside. | Shows the size and the number of items. | Read: `aicli_get_boot_space` |
| **Home** *name*: **data of deleted OpenCode workspaces** | Counts the OpenCode data of workspaces that are not in the workspace list or the favourites. Data of a workspace that exists is never counted. | Shows the size and the number of items. | Read: `aicli_get_boot_space` |
| **Home** *name*: **large Codex session logs** | Counts Codex session logs of 1 MB or more that did not change for 14 days. The size is also part of **conversation history**. | Shows the size and the number of items. | Read: `aicli_get_boot_space` |
| **Home** *name*: **large session logs of other agents** | Counts the sessions of Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Qwen Code, GitHub Copilot, Grok Build, Kimi Code and Antigravity CLI that are 1 MB or more in total and did not change for 14 days. The size is also part of **conversation history**. | Shows the size and the number of sessions. | Read: `aicli_get_boot_space` |
| **Left over**: **Archive layer images…** | Shows while old layer images are listed (**Old layer images that a newer merged layer replaced**). It opens the same dialog as **Archive…**. The plugin does not put an archived layer image back. | Dialog, then a background job. | Proposal only: `aicli_archive_boot_data` with the kind `superseded_layers` and the home name `all` |
| **Left over**: **Archived home data** | Shows the old or replaced home trees kept after a storage move. **Remove** deletes the listed archive after the plugin checks that it is not in use. You can also remove the archive by hand. | **Remove** confirm dialog, then the archive is removed. | No |
| **Archive…** | Opens a dialog. You pick a pool and a folder that already exists in it. The plugin copies each file to `<folder>/aicliagents-archive/<server name>/<date>/`, checks the copy, lists it in a manifest file, and then removes the file from the boot disk. It makes no new top-level folder on a pool. It refuses the boot disk, RAM, `/mnt/user` and the pool itself. | Starts a background job. The Activity tray shows the progress. | Proposal only: `aicli_archive_boot_data` |
| **Remove** | Opens a confirm dialog that names the items. It removes the listed data for good, with no copy. For archived home data, it removes that archive from its storage path. | Confirm dialog, then a background job. | Proposal only: `aicli_remove_boot_data` |

Both buttons leave an item alone when a program has one of its files open. They are grey during a storage migration.

| Control | What it does | At once | Agent |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| **Restore from an archive…** (bottom of the card) | Opens a dialog in three steps: pick the pool and the folder, pick an archive, then read a check that says how many files are new, the same or different. A different file is kept unless you choose **Replace them with the archived files**. Nothing is copied before you press **Restore**. | Dialog steps. The check and the restore run as background jobs. | None |
| **Keep the files in the home** / **Replace them with the archived files** | Your choice for files that are in the home with other content. The default is to keep them. | Sent with **Restore**. | None |

The card also warns early about a full boot disk. At 80 % it shows a warning in the card header and under the disk bar, and the Activity tray gets one notice. At 85 % the plugin also sends one Unraid notification in 6 hours. These limits are fixed. They have no setting.

### Actions on a home card

| Control | What it does | At once |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| **Save now** | Saves the unsaved changes of the home into a layer. While it runs, the card shows the percent ("Saving 35 %"), the size and the time left. | Confirm dialog "Persist Home Changes?" with the button **Persist Now**. |
| **Merge layers** | Saves unsaved changes and merges all layers into one. It is off when there is one layer and no unsaved change. While it runs, the card shows the percent and the Activity tray shows the step and the time left. | Asks you to confirm. Workspaces of the home pause and resume when it ends. |
| **Convert to plain folders** | Appears when the home has layers and its folder is not on a USB flash drive. It changes the home to plain folders in the same place. Then the home needs no more saves or tidy-ups. A home in plain folders has no **Save now** or **Merge layers** button. | Confirm dialog "Convert to plain folders?". Every workspace of the home closes and opens again. |
| **Remove old layers** | Appears on the home card only after a conversion to plain folders, while the plugin keeps the old layers for a rollback. The line next to it shows their size and the date of the automatic removal (14 days after the conversion). It removes them at once. | Confirm dialog "Remove old layers?" with the button **Remove**. |
| **Repair** | Appears when a home is not mounted. It unmounts and mounts the layers again. | Confirm dialog "Repair home storage?". It may briefly interrupt active sessions. |
| **Delete home…** (red) | Deletes the stored layers, settings and session data of the home. | Confirm dialog. For the primary user's home you must type DELETE. The deletion is permanent. |
| **Backup…** | Opens the backup dialog of this home. The row beside it reads \"Backup: …\" and has an **(i)**. The backup copies the home folder (agent settings, sign-ins and history). It does not copy the server. | Opens the dialog. |

> [!WARNING]
> **Delete home data** removes the layers, the settings and the session data of that home for good. A backup that you made to your own folder is not touched.

### Backup dialog (per home)

Each home has its own backup settings. The dialog shows the state of the last backup and saves each field at once, with "Saving…" and then "Saved" next to the field. The dialog shows the value the server read back, so what you see is what is saved. If a save fails, the field returns to the last saved value and shows "Not saved" with the reason.

| Setting | What it does | Default | Allowed values | When to change it | At once | Agent |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| **Destination folder** (**Choose folder…**) | Sets the folder that receives the backup copies. It must not be on a network or FUSE share. A /mnt/user folder is saved as its pool or disk path, because copying many small files through the share can freeze the server. | No folder chosen | A folder the plugin can use | Choose a folder on a different drive from the home storage. | Saves, then checks the folder and shows the resolved path and free space. If earlier backups exist in another folder, the dialog offers **Use this folder**. | No |
| **Mode** | Cold closes the home's sessions first, then relaunches them. It is the most consistent. Warm keeps sessions running and copies on a best-effort basis. | Cold | Cold; Warm | Choose Warm when you cannot close sessions. | Saves. | No |
| **Keep** | Sets how many snapshots to keep. The oldest go first. The plugin never removes the newest one. | 5 snapshots | A whole number from 1 to 50 | Raise it for a longer history. | Saves. | No |
| **Schedule** | Runs the backup by itself. | Off | Off; Daily at a time; Weekly on a day at a time (default time 02:00) | Choose a time when nobody uses the server. | Saves. The plugin updates its schedule job. | No |
| **Continue on relaunch** | Tells an agent to continue when it was working at the moment the backup started. | On | On; Off | Turn it off when you want to start agents yourself. | Saves. | No |
| **Advanced: excluded files** (**Excluded files, one pattern per line**) | Lists files the backup skips, for example caches you can download again. | Plugin caches and temporary files: .claude/plugins/**, **/node_modules/**, .grok/marketplace-cache/**, .gemini/antigravity-cli/**, .cache/**, .claude/image-cache/**, **/*.tmp | One pattern per line (letters, digits, . / * - _ and spaces) | Add a large folder that you do not need in the backup. | Saves when you leave the field. | No |
| **Back up now** | Starts a backup. | Disabled until you choose a folder | Not applicable | Before a risky change. | Confirm dialog. In Cold mode the home's sessions close first and relaunch after the copy. In Warm mode they keep running. | No (proposal only) |
| Snapshots list: **Restore…** and **Delete…** | Restores a snapshot, or deletes it. | Not applicable | Not applicable | Use **Restore…** after damage to a home. | Each asks you to confirm. A restore closes every session of that user, then reopens them. A session that was working is told to continue. | No (proposal only) |

> [!WARNING]
> **Restore…** replaces the home with the snapshot you choose. Changes made after the snapshot are lost. The plugin closes the user's sessions first and reopens them when the restore ends.

## Config Hub tab

See [Config Hub](config-hub.md). Set up your MCP servers, instructions, skills and commands once, and every agent that supports them gets them. The hub keeps one copy of your MCP servers, global instructions, skills and commands. It writes them into each agent's own configuration. The hub never touches entries that you created by hand in an agent's file. When the agent home is not mounted, a banner says **Apply to agents** is unavailable.

| Card and control | What it does | Default | At once |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| **MCP Servers**: **Add Server** | Opens the editor for one MCP server. Fields: **Name** (letters, digits, underscore, dash; up to 64), **Transport** (stdio, http or sse), **Command**, **Arguments (one per line)**, **Environment variables** (values are masked after saving; {SECRET_KEY} placeholders resolve from the secrets vault when applied), **URL** for http and sse, and **Enable for agents** (one tick per installed agent). | No servers | **Save Server** stores the definition. Nothing is written to an agent yet. |
| **MCP Servers** editor: **Authentication** (remote servers) | Chooses how the server checks who you are: **None**, **Bearer token** or **Custom header**. For a bearer token, type the secret key in braces, for example {MY_TOKEN}; the hub adds "Bearer ". For a custom header, type the header name and a value in braces. The hub refuses a typed token. Saved values show masked. | None | **Save Server** stores the key in braces only. **Apply to agents** writes the real value into each agent file. |
| **MCP Servers** editor: **Additional headers**, **Add header** (remote servers) | Extra request headers, such as a tenant number. A name that looks like a login (for example Authorization, X-API-Key, a name with token or secret) must hold a key in braces. Other values can be plain text. | No headers | **Save Server** stores them. **Apply to agents** writes them in the format of each agent. |
| **MCP Servers** editor: **Test connection** (remote servers) | The Unraid server connects to the URL with the values in the form and reports the HTTP status, a short fixed reason and the number of tools. It uses http or https only, follows no redirect and never shows the reply of the remote server. Nothing is saved. | Not applicable | Runs when you press it. |
| **MCP Servers**: **On** / **Off** button on a server row | Switches the server off for every agent, or on again. The agent ticks stay. A switched-off server shows the badge **off** and leaves the agent files at the next **Apply to agents**. | On | Saves at once. Nothing is written to an agent yet. |
| **MCP Servers**: **Apply to agents** | Writes each server into the config file of each ticked agent. | Not applicable | Writes the files. A running agent reads its servers when it starts. |
| **Config drift detected** (appears when needed) | A vendor file was edited outside the hub. Each row shows the file, the block, the state, and four buttons. **Compare** shows the text in the file next to the text of the hub. **Adopt** takes the edit into the hub. **Overwrite** puts the hub value back. **Release** stops managing the block or key. Point at a button to read what it does. A grey button does not work on that row, and its text says why. The hub never overwrites a drifted key by itself. | Not applicable | **Overwrite** always asks you to confirm. **Release** asks when it changes more than the one row, and names the agents it unticks. |
| **Global Instructions**: **Edit** (opens the text box, closed at first) and **Project to agents** ticks | Holds one instruction document that the hub writes into each ticked agent's instruction file, inside a marked block. Text outside the block is never touched. | Empty. No agent is ticked | **Apply to agents** writes the block. |
| **Skills & Commands**: **Add Skill**, **Add Command**, **Project skills to**, **Project commands to** | Hub-stored skills (a folder with a SKILL.md file) and slash commands (one markdown file). The hub copies them into agents that read them. It only changes the copies it made. | None. No agent is ticked | **Save Skill** and **Save Command** store the item. **Apply to agents** writes the copies. Delete asks you to confirm. |
| **History**: **Enable config backup** | Starts a git history of your agent configuration. A deny-by-default list tracks only allowed config files. Login and credential files can never enter it. Hub saves are committed after a short delay. | Off. It needs git on the server (install it with NerdTools) | Confirm dialog "Enable config backup?". |
| **History**: **Commit now**, a file's restore, **Restore settings** | Commit by hand, revert one file to an earlier version, or restore the plugin settings from the last backup. | Not applicable | Each shows a confirm dialog. **Restore settings** overwrites the live plugin settings on the flash drive with the last committed backup. Workspaces and the agent home are not changed. |
| **History**: **Remote URL (https)**, **Access token**, **Save remote**, **Push** | Sets an optional remote for the backup. A push is always manual. The token goes into the plugin's secrets vault and never into the URL. | No remote | **Save remote** stores the address. **Push** sends the backup. |

> [!WARNING]
> **Restore settings** replaces the plugin's live settings on the flash drive. Settings you changed after the last committed backup are lost. The restore itself leaves a record, so you can undo it.

## Agent Relay tab

See [Agent Relay](relay.md). Let your agents work together, with no need for you to pass messages by hand. The tab is one card. The header shows a status line, and the (i) button explains: agents share updates and send each other work requests through a shared mailbox. Messages go to each workspace's inbox. The plugin types a short notice into the agent's terminal so it reads the inbox; the wording is a setting on the Configuration tab. The sections below open and close. Relay is on from the first install.

| Section and setting | What it does | Default | Allowed values | When to change it | At once |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| **Connect another machine**: **Allow other machines to connect** | Lets agents on other computers join the Relay over an encrypted connection. A fresh install opens no listener and creates no token. | Off | On; Off | Turn it on when an agent on another computer must reach this Relay. Treat each token like a password. | Nothing, until you press **Apply**. |
| **Port** | Sets the port of the listener. | 8237 | 1024 to 65535 | Change it when another service uses the port. | Nothing, until **Apply**. |
| **Listen on** | Sets the address the listener binds to. | 0.0.0.0 (every interface) | An IP address | Enter one address to limit where the listener answers. | Nothing, until **Apply**. |
| **Apply** | Applies the three settings above. | Not applicable | Not applicable | After a change. | Starts or stops the listener at once and shows the endpoint address. |
| **Remotes**: **New remote name**, **Add remote** | Makes one remote (an outside machine or agent) with its own access token. A remote shows to your workspaces as a contact. | None | Text, up to 40 characters | Make one remote for each machine. | Creates the remote and its token. |
| A remote's **Permissions**, **Copy**, **Rotate**, **Rename**, **Remove** | **Permissions** sets what the remote may do. **Copy** copies the token. **Rotate** replaces the token, and the old one stops working. **Remove** deletes the remote and its token. | A remote may read its own inbox, see the list of workspaces and send private messages | See the permissions dialog below | Remove access you no longer need. | **Rotate** and **Remove** stop the old token at once. |
| **Linked boxes**: **Allow linked boxes**, **Apply** | Lets workspaces on this Unraid box and on another box that runs the plugin send each other private messages. It needs **Allow other machines to connect** on both boxes. | Off | On; Off | Turn it on to link two boxes. | Saves when you press **Apply**. Links and messages are kept when you turn it off. |
| **Link a box**, **Enter a pairing code**, **Check code**, **Link** | Pair two boxes with a one-time code that lasts 15 minutes. **Cancel code** cancels it early. | Not applicable | Not applicable | Use them once for each pair of boxes. | **Check code** shows what the code links to and lets you edit the address of the other box. **Link** pairs the boxes. |
| **Topics**: **New topic name**, **Description (optional)**, **Add topic** | Topics are the channels agents subscribe to. Built-in topics cannot be edited. | The built-in topics | Lowercase dot-separated names, up to 128 characters, for example local.llm.health | Add a topic for a job that several agents share. | **Add topic** creates it. **Archive** stops new messages and keeps the history, after a confirm dialog. An archived topic shows a **Remove** button. |
| **Mirror notifications into the Relay** | Copies this plugin's Unraid notifications to the fixed topic platform.unraid.notification so agents see them. | On | On; Off | Turn it off when agents should not see Unraid notifications. | Saves when you press **Apply**. |
| **Topic owners**: **Owner workspace**, **Start at boot** | The owner is the one workspace that answers work requests for a topic. It is subscribed by itself. **Start at boot** starts that workspace when the server starts. **Start now** starts it at once. | No owner. Start at boot off | No owner, or any workspace in the drawer | Name an owner when one agent is responsible for a service. | Saves as you change it. Saving an owner also starts that workspace when it is stopped. |
| **Activity**: **Send a test message** (**Topic**, **Importance**, **Message**, **Send**) | Sends a test message to check that subscriptions and inboxes work. It cannot run commands. | Importance: Info | Info; Warning; Critical | After a change to topics or owners. | Sends the message. It shows in the list. |
| **Activity**: **Show**, **Refresh** | Chooses how many past messages the list shows. | Latest 100 | Latest 25; Latest 100; Latest 250 | Raise it to look further back. | Reloads the list. |
| **Advanced**: **Give agents built-in Relay tools** | Installs the Relay tools into every supported agent. Turning it off removes the tools at each workspace's next start. Agents can still use the Relay command line. | On | On; Off | Turn it off when you do not want the Relay tools in your agents. | Saves when you press **Apply**. A box lists the running workspaces that still use the old tools, each with a **Restart** button. |

The **Permissions** dialog for a linked box has these controls. The server checks every grant again.

| Control | What it does | Default |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| **Allow private messages to this box's workspaces** | Lets the other box send private messages to your workspaces. | On |
| **Workspaces the other box can see** | Chooses All saved workspaces, Only the workspaces I choose, or None. | All saved workspaces |
| **Messages and calls a minute (1–600)** | Limits the rate of the link. | 120 for a linked box; 30 for a remote |

The **Permissions** dialog for a remote has these controls.

| Control | What it does | Default |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| **Read its own inbox** | The remote reads the messages sent to it. | On |
| **See the list of workspaces** | The remote sees the contacts. | On |
| **Send private messages to workspaces** | The remote sends direct messages. | On |
| **Requests to topic actors** (one tick per topic) | The remote sends work requests to the actor of a ticked topic and reads their status. Only the actor acts. Request text is data, never a command. | Off for every topic |
| **May cancel its own requests** | The remote cancels requests it made. | Off |

## Debug Console tab

See [Health, Activity and troubleshooting](health-and-troubleshooting.md). The tab shows the plugin's logs. The coloured **Health** dot above the tabs belongs to the same area. Press the (i) next to it to see which checks are not fine, and click the dot to open this tab.

| Control | What it does | Default | Allowed values | At once |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| Log tabs: **Debug**, **Migration**, **Install**, **Uninstall** | Choose which log to read. Debug is the live activity log. Migration is the log of the last settings upgrade. Install and Uninstall are the logs of the last install and removal. | Debug | Debug; Migration; Install; Uninstall | Shows that log. The filters hide for the Install and Uninstall logs. |
| **Context** | Shows only the lines from one part of the plugin. | All | All, or one of the parts that appear in the log | Reloads the log. |
| **Level** | Shows only lines at or above a severity. | All | All; ERR! only; WARN+; INFO+; DBUG+ | Reloads the log. |
| **Trace** | Narrows the log to one trace id, so you can follow one action from start to end. | Empty | A trace id of up to 16 characters | Reloads the log. |
| **Tail** | Sets how many of the newest lines load. | 500 | 100; 500; 1000; 2000 | Reloads the log. |
| **Reset filters** (undo icon) | Puts the four filters back to their defaults. | Not applicable | Not applicable | Reloads the log. |
| **Paused** marker | Appears while your pointer is over the log. New lines wait until you move the pointer away. | Not applicable | Not applicable | Not applicable. |
| **Copy to Clipboard** (copy icon) | Copies the shown log. | Not applicable | Not applicable | Copies. |
| **Clear Log** (eraser icon) | Empties the selected log. | Not applicable | Not applicable | Confirm dialog "Clear … log?" with the button **Yes, Clear It**. This cannot be undone. |
| **Support** menu: **Download support bundle**, **Copy forum post**, **Create GitHub issue**, **Check known issues** | Build a zip of logs and configuration with secrets removed. Copy a short summary for the Unraid forum. Open a prefilled GitHub issue (nothing posts until you send it). Fetch the list of known issues and match it against your recent logs. | Not applicable | Not applicable | Each action runs when you press it. Nothing sends by itself. |
| **Strict anonymize** (in the Support menu) | Replaces share names, the host name and LAN addresses in the bundle. | Off | On; Off | Applies to the next bundle. |
| **Performance trace** (tick box in the Support menu) | Writes a timing line for each slow step, such as a slow request, a slow Notebook scan or a slow check of the home mount. The lines go to a separate performance log, and a short WARN line goes to the Debug log. Use it while you look for a page that hangs. | Off | On; Off | Saves. The server follows at once. Pages that are already open follow when you reload them. |

## Switches in the terminal drawer

The terminal page has its own switches in the workspace drawer. They are not on the Settings page. See [Workspaces](workspaces.md), [The terminal](terminal.md) and [Workspace settings and automation](workspace-settings-and-automation.md).

| Switch | What it does | Default | Where the choice lives | At once | Agent |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| **Pin drawer open** / **Unpin drawer** (thumb-tack icon) | Keeps the drawer open beside the terminal. While it is pinned, clicking a workspace does not close the drawer. | Unpinned | This browser | Saves in this browser. | No |
| **Voice: on (all devices)** / **Voice: off (all devices)** (speaker icon) | The same switch as **Voice** on the Configuration tab. | Off | The plugin settings. It applies to every device | Saves. Every open tab updates. | Yes |
| **Dictate to the active workspace (Ctrl+Shift+M)** (microphone icon) | Starts and stops dictation into the open workspace. The icon pulses while it records. It shows only when a workspace is open. The icon changes to a crossed microphone when voice input is refused. | Not recording | Not stored | Starts or stops recording. The browser may ask for microphone permission the first time. | No |
| Notebook **Pin beside the terminal** / **Unpin** | Keeps the Notebook open beside the terminal. | Unpinned | This browser, for each workspace | Saves in this browser. | No |
| Notebook **Project** / **Global** | Chooses the notebook of the project folder, or the Global notebook for notes that belong to no project. | Project | This browser, for each workspace | Switches the list. | No |
| Notebook width | You drag the edge of the Notebook to set its width. | 420 pixels | This browser, for each workspace | Saves in this browser. The width stays between 340 and 720 pixels. | No |
| Notebook **Notebook settings** (in the **More** menu) | Opens the Notebook card on the Configuration tab. | Not applicable | Not applicable | Opens the Settings page. | No |

### Switches in a workspace's "..." menu

Open the "..." menu of a workspace row to reach these. On a phone, the menu rows are large enough to touch.

| Switch | What it does | Default | At once | Agent |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| **Voice**: **Speak** / **Voice mail** / **Off** | Speak reads this workspace's messages aloud and keeps them in voice mail. Voice mail keeps them without speaking. Off stops this workspace from speaking, and nothing is kept. | Speak | Saves in the workspace record. It applies on every device. | Yes |
| **Voice**: **Spoken name…** | Sets the name each spoken message starts with ("<name> says:"). Empty uses the workspace name. **Use the workspace name** clears it. | The workspace name | Saves when you press the confirm button. Up to 40 characters. | Yes |
| **Voice**: **Voice…** (**Voice**, **Speed**, **Test**) | Chooses a voice and a speed for this workspace. They win over the Settings voice. Speed is available only when a natural voice engine is set. | Default (the Settings voice and speed) | **Save** applies at once. **Test** plays a sample in this browser only. Speed range: 0.5 to 2.0. | Yes |
| **Continue**: **Schedule…** (**When**, **Repeat**) | Continues this workspace by itself at a time you choose, for example when its usage quota resets. It fires only when the agent is ready for input. | No schedule | **Save** sets the schedule. **Cancel schedule** removes it. Repeat: Once; Every day; Every week. | Yes |
| **Relay**: **Settings** (**Allow this agent to manage only its own subscriptions**, **Trust private Relay messages as terminal notifications**) | Sets how this workspace takes part in the Relay. | Both on | **Save subscriptions** saves. | No |

## If something goes wrong

| What you see | What it means | What to do |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| A setting jumps back to its old value after a dialog. | You pressed **Cancel**, pressed Escape or clicked outside the dialog. Or the check refused the change. | Read the message in the dialog. Change the setting again when you are ready. |
| The page shows "Saved" but a terminal looks the same. | **Colour scheme** and **Text size** apply when a terminal loads. | Reload the page. |
| A running agent does not see a change to tools, Relay or an environment variable. | An agent reads its tools and environment when it starts. | Restart the workspace. The Relay tab lists the workspaces that still use the old tools. |
| A voice field does not save. | The field shows the reason in red. | Fix the value (for example a speed outside 0.5 to 2.0) and leave the field again. |
| **Back up now** is greyed out. | The home has no destination folder, or a backup or restore is running. | Choose a folder in the dialog, or wait. |
| A storage move fails. | The target is too full, not available or not allowed. | Read the dialog. The setting returns to the old value and nothing is deleted. See [Health, Activity and troubleshooting](health-and-troubleshooting.md). |

- [Workspace settings and automation](workspace-settings-and-automation.md): launch arguments, environment variables, auto-launch and the Continue automations of one workspace.
- [The terminal](terminal.md): theme, font, copy and paste, uploads and touch controls.
- [Voice](voice.md): speech, dictation and voice mail.
- [The Notebook](notebook.md): the Notebook drawer and its settings.
- [Home and agent storage](storage.md): where homes and agents live, and how to move or merge them.
- [Home backup and restore](backup-restore.md): the per-home backup and restore.
- [Agent Store](agent-store.md): install, upgrade and configure agents.
- [Config Hub](config-hub.md): MCP servers, instructions, skills and commands for all agents.
- [Agent Relay](relay.md): topics, owners, remotes and linked boxes.
- [Plugin management tools for agents](agent-tools.md): what an agent may read, change or propose.
- [Health, Activity and troubleshooting](health-and-troubleshooting.md): the Health dot, the Activity tray and the Debug Console.

- **2026-10-22** — The Configuration tab has nine cards: **General**, **Storage**, **Terminal**, **Automatic continue**, **Relay notices**, **Agent voice**, **Dictation**, **Notebook** and **SSH keys**. Seldom-used settings are in a closed **Advanced** part of each card. The patterns and the Terminal input safety rules are the **Advanced** part of **Automatic continue**. **Save unsaved home changes every** is hidden when every home is a plain folder. Your browser maps a saved card layout to the new cards. Spec `docs/specs/SETTINGS_PAGE_FIRST_CLASS_REDESIGN.md`, issue #750.
